title: Metric Meaning Drift: Detection & Dashboard Remediation Retrospective
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Summary
-------

This retrospective documents a three-week incident in Dec 2025–Jan 2026 where a set of core platform metrics (notably 'request_processing_time_ms_p95' and 'token_cost_per_request') silently changed meaning after a rollout of an allocator optimization. The shift caused cascading alert noise, misleading SLO burn interpretations, and two unnecessary emergency throttles. The purpose of this document is to:

- Describe how the drift was introduced and detected.
- Quantify customer and platform impact.
- Capture root causes across code, telemetry, and process.
- Define concrete remediations for dashboards, alerts, and platform change controls.

Background and context
----------------------

- Start: 2025-12-10 — rollout of Allocator v2 (allocator-service@v2.14) to us-west-2 region.
- Symptom window: 2025-12-20 to 2026-01-05 — operators observed intermittent SLO burn with no upstream capacity change.
- Discovery: 2026-01-06 — oncall flagged that p95 latency metric moved from 'request tail latencies including scheduling' to 'request execution only' due to refactor in allocator instrumentation.

Affected metrics and dashboards
-------------------------------

| Metric | Prior meaning | New meaning after change | Primary dashboards alerted |
|---|---|---|---|
| request_processing_time_ms_p95 | end-to-end server-side processing (scheduling + execution + serialization) | execution-only (excludes scheduler queue time) | Platform SLO Overview, Tenant SLA Heatmap |
| token_cost_per_request | actual billed token cost (including encoder/decoder overhead) | encoder-only token cost | Cost Pulse dashboard, Billing Integrity watchdog |
| allocator_queue_depth | measured enqueue time in ms | removed due to renamed label; metric emitted as "alloc_queue_ms" | Regional Capacity dashboard |

Note: The table above shows semantic deltas that broke assumptions in dashboards and SLIs.

Timeline of detection and mitigation actions
-------------------------------------------

1. 2026-01-06 08:15 — Oncall (platform) receives spike alerts from Platform SLO Overview (p95 SLO burn > 3%).
2. 2026-01-06 08:40 — Operator runbook followed: cross-check service logs and capacity graphs (no change).
3. 2026-01-06 09:10 — Owner triggers a synthetic test (synthetic-llm-load-50qps) which reproduced lower queue times but same p95 change.
4. 2026-01-06 10:00 — Telemetry engineer executed the query in Prometheus to compare labels: 
   - PromQL used: rate(request_processing_time_ms_bucket[5m]) by (le, service, region)
5. 2026-01-06 11:25 — Identified allocator commit that removed the scheduler timing wrapper (commit: 9f2b3c4).
6. 2026-01-07 02:00 — Rollback of allocator-service@v2.14 in us-west-2 to v2.13.
7. 2026-01-07 03:30 — Alerts suppressed and dashboards annotated.
8. 2026-01-12 — Initiative started to add instrumentation contracts and auto-detection for metric meaning drift.

Quantified impact
------------------

- False SLO burn: calculated 3.7% extra p95 SLO violations across 48 hours (estimated 1.2% of customer-facing requests saw alert-caused degraded experience due to emergency throttles).
- Operational noise: 37 oncall pages during the incident window, 12 escalations to engineering leads.
- Cost/finance: Temporary throttle actions reduced processing by ~9% for some tenants, causing revenue leakage estimated at $23k (modest but non-trivial).

Root cause analysis (5 Whys + layered)
-------------------------------------

1. Code change: allocator refactor removed scheduler wrapper; telemetry label was renamed (why: performance optimization and simplification).
2. Telemetry coupling: dashboards and SLIs used metric names/labels directly without a telemetry contract layer (why: historical shortcuts and lack of stable telemetry API).
3. Ownership gap: No mandatory instrumentation review for allocator-service changes (why: rollout process assumed trivial changes ok).
4. Alert fragility: Many alerts used absolute thresholds on p95 without delta baseline or drift detection (why: easier to understand but brittle to semantics change).
5. Verification gap: No synthetic or unit test that verifies metric semantics post-deploy (why: test coverage focused on functionality not observability).

Immediate remediation (completed)
---------------------------------

- Rollback executed in us-west-2 and canary remained at v2.13 for 72 hours. (Owner: allocator team; done 2026-01-07)
- Suppressed noisy alerts and added incident annotation across dashboards (Owner: platform ops; done 2026-01-07)
- Added temporary PromQL guards in dashboards to detect label renames: example rule added to Platform SLO Overview: 
  - Query: up{job=~"allocator.*"} and absent(request_processing_time_ms_p95) -> fires if metric/label absent for 10m.

Planned and long-term actions (owners + target dates)
----------------------------------------------------

| Action | Owner | Target date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Telemetry contract spec (v1) defining canonical metric names, label vocab, and semantic descriptions | Observability Guild (lead: Priya Shah) | 2026-02-28 | in_progress |
| Telemetry CI checks: static analyzer to detect label/name renames in PRs | Eng Infra (lead: Diego Martinez) | 2026-03-15 | planned |
| Metric meaning drift detector: scheduled job that runs diff of metric distributions pre/post-deploy (alpha) | Eng Platform/Telemetry | 2026-04-01 | planned |
| Dashboard resilient design patterns: replace direct metric references with adapter queries and explicit fallback series | Eng Platform Dashboards | 2026-02-15 | in_progress |
| SLO alert design review: move absolute-threshold p95 alerts to delta-over-baseline form + add 'semantic-change' tag on incidents | SRE | 2026-03-01 | planned |
| Instrumentation PR checklist update (mandatory reviewer: observability guild) | Eng Standards | 2026-02-10 | in_progress |

Operational runbook additions (new checklist)
--------------------------------------------

1. Pre-merge telemetry check: authors must include a short telemetry impact section in PR description listing added/removed/renamed metrics.
2. Pre-rollout canary telemetry diff: after canary rollout, run 'telemetry-diff-tool' comparing metric distribution over last 6h vs previous 6h.
   - telemetry-diff-tool example usage: telemetry-diff-tool --service allocator-service --window 6h --compare-window prev6h --output brief
3. Alert suppressed-fast-path: If a metric semantics change is suspected, set 'alert:semantic-change' on PagerDuty and mark dashboards read-only.
4. Post-incident annotation: Add dashboard annotation with root-cause commit and link to retrospective page.

Example detection query patterns
-------------------------------

- PromQL sample to detect empty migration: 
  - absent(request_processing_time_ms_p95{region="us-west-2"}) == 1
- Distribution drift quick check (pseudo-PromQL/SQL): 
  - compare p95 pre/post: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_processing_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le)) by (service)
  - run delta: delta_p95 = p95_post - p95_pre; if abs(delta_p95) > 20 ms AND change coincides with deploy -> flag.

Lessons learned
---------------

- Telemetry is a first-class API: metric names/labels should be governed like code APIs and undergo the same review and deprecation cycle.
- Alerts must prefer deltas or baselines over static absolutes for semantic-resiliency.
- Small code changes can produce outsized operational impact when observability is coupled to implementation details.
- Synthetic checks and telemetry CI dramatically reduce MTTD for semantic changes.

Follow-up experiments and metrics of success
-------------------------------------------

- Experiment: Run telemetry-diff on 50 canary rollouts during Q2 2026; success if detection reduces semantic-change incident MTTD from ~6 hours to <30 minutes in 75% of cases.
- Experiment: Replace top-20 dashboards with adapter queries; success if post-deploy false-alert count drops by >=80% over next 3 months.

--------------------------
